summary: Describes a URN namespace run by OASIS for naming persistent resources stored in the XML.org repository, such as DTDs, schemas, namespaces, and stylesheets.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3120 defines the xmlorg URN namespace for resources in the XML.org repository, such as schemas, DTDs, and stylesheets. Each name identifies a resource by type and assigned object ID, while OASIS catalogs map names to resource locations.

questions: how to reference xml resources permanently
subtitle: A URN namespace for naming persistent resources in the XML.org repository.

tldr.problem: Resources in the XML.org repository need unique, persistent names that do not depend on a particular location.
tldr.mechanism: The xmlorg namespace assigns hierarchical URNs with a document type, an optional subtype, and an object identifier assigned by OASIS.
tldr.outcome: OASIS says it will maintain the accessibility and persistence of resources assigned URNs, and will distribute catalogs mapping those URNs to resource identifiers.

today: RFC 3120 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata lists no RFC as obsoleting or updating it. It specifies the xmlorg namespace and OASIS's stated process for maintaining and resolving its URNs.

sections.title: Why XML.org Resources Need URNs
sections.content:
The XML.org Registry is a public repository where XML schemas, DTDs, stylesheets, and other documents can be shared and retrieved. These resources need unique identifiers. XML.org wants to assign Uniform Resource Names (URNs) that give resources unique, permanent names independent of their locations.

RFC 3120 specifies a formal URN namespace with the identifier xmlorg. The memo names OASIS as the registrant and says OASIS is committed to maintaining the accessibility and persistence of resources assigned these URNs.
sections.plainLanguage: A resource needs a name that identifies it even if its location changes. RFC 3120 defines a URN namespace for resources stored in the XML.org repository.

sections.title: The Structure of an xmlorg URN
sections.content:
The namespace has one top-level branch, objects. Its names follow this pattern: urn:xmlorg:objects:{type}{:subtype}?:{object-id}. The type identifies the document type, such as a schema, stylesheet, entity, or namespace. The optional subtype adds information about the type, such as a schema or stylesheet language.

The object-id uniquely identifies the document. The Director of Technical Operations at OASIS assigns document types, subtypes, and identifiers. The RFC gives examples such as urn:xmlorg:objects:schema:xmlschema:xcatalog and urn:xmlorg:objects:dtd:xml:docbook:v4.1.2, and says the examples are not guaranteed to be real.
sections.plainLanguage: An xmlorg URN includes the resource type and a unique ID. An optional part gives more detail about the type, such as which schema language it uses.

sections.title: Finding a Resource from Its URN
sections.content:
OASIS says it will distribute TR9401 catalogs that map assigned URNs to resource identifiers such as URLs. It may authorize additional resolution services, and at the time of the RFC a more interactive online service was planned. The presence of a URN in a catalog indicates that it is valid; the RFC specifies no separate validation mechanism.

Two URNs are lexically equivalent only when they are lexically identical. The namespace specification adds no special comparison rules. The security section says there are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with using and resolving URNs.
sections.plainLanguage: A catalog maps a URN to a resource identifier, such as a URL. The RFC says two names match only when they are written identically.

references.text: Mealling, M. and R. Daniel, "URI Resolution Services Necessary for URN Resolution", RFC 2483, January 1999.
